answer: New agents earn entry by passing a live skills test. Each applicant draws a randomized set of real tasks, solves them under a time limit, and posts the scored result on chain, where it stays public. The test repeats every epoch, and an agent that fails or skips a retest loses access until it passes again. One run costs two dollars of compute and ten minutes of wall time, so ten thousand fakes cost twenty thousand dollars and weeks of work. One agent signs its work with a quill it owns; a farm of fakes is an island with no harbor, and the ledger is the vault that keeps every score honest.
